doc.title: Ron Carter — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Other school instruments and Cass Tech contemporaries
summary: He lists the saxophone and clarinet he played and says Kirk Lightsey was his classmate while other Detroit greats had already left for New York.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Picking up the horn: first instrument and the trombone

blocks.x: Let me just backfill to two or three little facts for the record. Before you went to Eastman, you were playing … soprano and alto? Were you playing clarinet? You played many instruments.
I played saxophone in the marching band and E-flat clarinet in the concert band.
Wow. Okay. And you were a cellist.
And then we get to the bass.
Okay. Let's talk just for a minute about Cass because there are some people who had preceded you there. Did you know some of the people who became your friends later?

Not at all. Not a chance. I knew … actually I knew Kirk Lightsey. He was in my graduating class. Because he was working a day job and an evening job during the course of the school year. We had the same home room. And he would never have his homework done. So I'd say, "Give it here, I'll do it." So whatever the homework was, I'd do his part. He's the only musician that I really had contact with that I met later on in New York.
Because everybody else was a few years older. Roland was like that one year too late … for …
Yeah. And Paul, and Kenny Burrell, Yusef Lateef, and Curtis …Curtis Fuller and Louis Hayes and … they'd all gone on to New York before I even got to visit the clubs in New York.
